newsitem.title: MEXICO: Lucent shifting phone production to Mexico.
newsitem.headline: Lucent shifting phone production to Mexico.

text.p: U.S.-based telecommunications company Lucent Technologies Inc will shift all of its world telephone production to its plant in the western Mexico city of Guadalajara by 2000, a plant director said late Tuesday.
"Before this century ends, we are going to be producing in this state (of Jalisco) ... 100 percent of production," Carlos Bue, director general of the Guadalajara plant, told reporters.
"After representing 10 percent of (the company's) production (in 1991), this year we are producing for 85 percent of world demand and next year it will be 95 percent," he said.
Bue spoke to reporters ahead of President Ernesto Zedillo's scheduled visit to the plant on Wednesday afternoon to inaugurate a new plant expansion.
The six-year-old plant currently makes about 12 million telephones a year.
With the shift to Mexico, Lucent will stop using Asian subcontractors, Bue siad.
"Basically, the reason is quality, the quality of the product here versus there," Bue said.
Production in Guadalajara includes 60 different models ranging from basic telephones to more sophisticated digital and wireless units.
